title: Menilai Argumen dan Kredibilitas Informasi
summary: High-level cognitive evaluation: fact-checking assertions, assessing institutional authority and methodology, identifying cognitive bias, and judging information sufficiency.

lessons.title: The CRAAP Framework: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose

blocks.html:
Information Verification: The CRAAP Test

In an era saturated with algorithmic misinformation, sponsored native advertising, and unverified viral claims, the TKA Tingkat Lanjut exam places paramount importance on critical source evaluation.

Developed by librarians at California State University, Chico, the CRAAP Framework is the premier academic standard for evaluating information reliability.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Spotting Disinformation in the Digital Deluge
blocks.html: When you read a health blog claiming that drinking celery juice cures terminal cancer, how do you verify its credibility? Is the information recent? Who wrote it—a licensed oncologist or an influencer selling juice blenders? The CRAAP Framework is the premier analytical rubric utilized by top university research libraries worldwide to evaluate information credibility.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Sarah Blakeslee and the Meriam Library CRAAP Test
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Sarah Blakeslee Tahun: 2004 M Krisis: Internet users cite blog posts written by anonymous internet users with commercial sales agendas as if they were peer-reviewed scientific studies.

Librarian Sarah Blakeslee and her team at California State University, Chico (2004) developed the CRAAP test to equip university students with a rigorous mental checklist against digital disinformation and sponsored propaganda.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: The Five Pillars of the CRAAP Rubric
blocks.html:
1. Currency: The timeliness of the information (publication date, revisions).
2. Relevance: The importance of the information for your research needs and appropriate academic depth.
3. Authority: The credentials, institutional affiliations, and scholarly expertise of the author/publisher.
4. Accuracy: Textual reliability, empirical verification, peer-review status, and citation rigor.
5. Purpose: The underlying motive behind the publication (to inform, educate, sell, persuade, or entertain; detecting hidden bias).

blocks.title: The CRAAP Diagnostic Matrix for Critical Reading
blocks.html:
Currency → Authority → Accuracy → Purpose
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
CurrencyWhen was the study conducted? Has subsequent data disproven it?Temporal validity
AuthorityDoes the author possess verifiable credentials in this scientific domain?Authorial credibility
AccuracyAre assertions substantiated by replicable citations and data methodology?Verifiable truth-value
PurposeIs there a conflict of interest or undisclosed commercial funding?Dispassionate objectivity

Pedagogical Note: In advanced TKA questions regarding source credibility: Eliminate sources lacking author credentials or displaying evident financial bias.

blocks.title: Simulasi Interaktif: Evaluasi Kredibilitas Sumber Berbasis Skor CRAAP
blocks.caption: Uji ketajaman Anda menilai kelayakan berbagai artikel jurnal dan laporan media online.

blocks.title: Deteksi Domain Situs Web
blocks.html:
• .edu / .ac.id: Institusi pendidikan tinggi dan riset universitas (kredibilitas akademis tinggi).
  • .gov / .go.id: Lembaga pemerintah resmi (data sensus dan undang-undang resmi).
  • .org: Organisasi nirlaba (periksa apakah netral atau lembaga lobi politik partisan).
  • .com: Entitas komersial (waspadai motif penjualan produk dan iklan terselubung).

blocks.title: Applied Analytical Scenario: The CRAAP Framework: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose
blocks.question: How can a critical reader analyze and verify discourse arguments regarding 'The CRAAP Framework: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose' based on principles articulated by Sarah Blakeslee?

steps.step: Identify Textual Claims and Operational Constraints
steps.explanation: Examine the core assertions in the target text and locate the explicit warrants connecting premises to the central thesis of The CRAAP Framework: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose.

steps.step: Evaluate Evidence Quality and Rhetorical Framing
steps.explanation: Cross-examine whether the supporting data meets scholarly standards, checking for potential logical fallacies or biases.

steps.step: Synthesize Authorial Stance and Strategic Implications
steps.explanation: Determine the underlying communicative purpose and synthesize actionable conclusions aligned with Sarah Blakeslee's framework.

blocks.answer: By systematically evaluating textual evidence and logical structure, readers can resolve complex comprehension challenges regarding The CRAAP Framework: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose with critical confidence.

blocks.title: Comprehension Check: The CRAAP Framework: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose
blocks.question: Which of the following statements most accurately reflects the core principle established by Sarah Blakeslee regarding 'The CRAAP Framework: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose'?

options.A: The concept relies entirely on subjective guesswork without requiring any textual or empirical justification.
options.B: The principle provides a rigorous analytical framework grounded in verifiable evidence and coherent logical relations.
options.C: The rule is completely obsolete and has been universally rejected by all modern academic institutions.
options.D: The structure can only be applied when reading ancient fictional poetry and is invalid for academic prose.
options.E: The framework mandates that readers must accept all internet claims without checking author credibility.

blocks.explanation: Option B is correct. In academic discourse, The CRAAP Framework: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose establishes systematic criteria for rigorous critical analysis. Option A is incorrect because validity requires evidence. Option C is false as the framework remains foundational. Option D is incorrect because it applies across academic genres. Option E contradicts the principles of critical evaluation.
blocks.hint: Identify the option emphasizing evidence-based reasoning, logical consistency, and scholarly integrity.

lessons.title: Assessing Peer-Review Status, Citations, and Domain Competence

blocks.html:
Domain Competence and the Gold Standard of Peer Review

Not all experts are created equal. A Nobel laureate in Theoretical Physics does not possess automatic institutional authority on pediatric vaccines. In TKA critical items, you must evaluate domain competence (apakah keahlian sang narasumber sesuai dengan bidang yang sedang diperdebatkan) and peer-review status.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: The Gold Standard of Scientific Truth
blocks.html: Why do university professors and Nobel Prize committees insist on Peer-Reviewed sources? Because in science, an author cannot just print whatever they want. Before publication in a reputable journal, their data, methodology, mathematical calculations, and lab samples are rigorously cross-examined and challenged by independent, anonymous world experts in that exact specialty.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Henry Oldenburg and Philosophical Transactions 1665
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Henry Oldenburg Tahun: 1665 M Krisis: Readers treat a self-published viral tweet with equal authority as a paper scrutinized and verified by double-blind referee panels.

In 1665, Henry Oldenburg, secretary of the Royal Society of London, founded the Philosophical Transactions, instituting the world's first formal system of peer review to ensure that scientific claims were authenticated by independent scholars before publication.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Double-Blind Peer Review and Citation Metrics
blocks.html: Peer Review is the evaluation of scholarly work by one or more people with similar competence as the producers of the work (peers). Citation Impact / H-index indicates how frequently subsequent independent researchers have relied upon, replicated, and built upon those published findings.

blocks.title: Hierarchy of Source Credibility in Academic English
blocks.html:
Tier 1: Top-Tier Peer-Reviewed Journals → Tier 2: University Press & Gov Reports → Tier 3: Mainstream Respected Journalism → Tier 4: Blogs & Social Media Posts
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Tier 1: Top-Tier Peer-Reviewed JournalsNature, Science, The Lancet, IEEE Transactions (Rigorous double-blind review)Highest academic authority
Tier 2: University Press & Gov ReportsOxford University Press, WHO Reports, National Bureau of Economic ResearchHigh institutional credibility
Tier 3: Mainstream Respected JournalismBBC, The Economist, Financial Times, National GeographicReliable secondary analysis
Tier 4: Blogs & Social Media PostsSelf-published medium articles, Twitter threads, promotional sponsored contentZero academic verification

Pedagogical Note: In reading tests: An argument derived from a peer-reviewed academic journal consistently outranks commercial website blogs in credibility.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Otoritas Pakar Domain
blocks.question: A software engineer with 2 million YouTube followers publishes a video asserting that a specific herbal tea eradicates pancreatic cancer tumors. Should this claim be deemed scientifically credible?
steps: Evaluasi Domain: Narasumber adalah insinyur perangkat lunak (software engineer), bukan dokter onkologi atau peneliti farmakologi klinis.
Evaluasi Metodologi: Tidak ada uji klinis tersamar ganda (double-blind randomized trial) yang diterbitkan di jurnal medis terindeks peer-review.
Media Publikasi: Video media sosial yang monetisasi klik, bukan jurnal sains.
Kesimpulan: Klaim tersebut tidak memiliki kredibilitas ilmiah dan merupakan contoh Appeal to False Authority.
blocks.answer: Klaim tersebut tidak kredibel karena tidak bersumber dari pakar onkologi dan tidak melewati uji klinis peer-review.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: What makes an article published in a double-blind peer-reviewed journal far more trustworthy than a viral blog post?

options.A: The journal uses brighter photographic illustrations.
options.B: Independent domain experts evaluated the methodology, data accuracy, and ethical compliance prior to publication.
options.C: The journal is completely free of charge to all readers worldwide.
options.D: The blog post author has more social media followers.

blocks.hint: Peer-review memastikan naskah diaudit oleh pakar independen sebelum terbit.
blocks.explanation: Jurnal peer-review mewajibkan audit metodologis, verifikasi akurasi data statistik, dan penelaahan kritis oleh para pakar independen sebelum disetujui untuk terbit (Pilihan B).

lessons.title: Recognizing Confirmation Bias, Framing Effects, and Emotional Manipulation

blocks.html:
Psychological Blindspots: Cognitive Biases in Reading Stimuli

Human beings are not dispassionate computing engines. Authors (and readers) are vulnerable to cognitive biases that systematically distort how information is gathered, interpreted, and recalled.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Why Smart People Believe Questionable Claims
blocks.html: Have you ever noticed that people instantly share articles whose headlines align with their personal opinions, without even reading past the first paragraph? Human cognition is hardwired with mental shortcuts (heuristics) that can easily warp our reading comprehension into biased self-confirmation.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Kahneman and Tversky on Judgment Under Uncertainty
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Daniel Kahneman & Amos Tversky Tahun: 1974 M Krisis: Readers fall into cognitive traps, accepting claims that confirm their pre-existing prejudices while ignoring contradictory data.

Psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky published their groundbreaking paper Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases in Science (1974). Their work founded behavioral economics, proving that systematic cognitive distortions systematically warp human reasoning across all domains.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Cognitive Bias in Reading and Information Processing
blocks.html: A Cognitive Bias is a systematic deviation from normative rationality in judgment, causing individuals to perceive reality through distorted psychological filters.

blocks.title: Cognitive Bias Diagnostics in Reading Comprehension
blocks.html:
Examine Stimulus Claims → Identify Psychological Trigger → Audit Data Objectivity → Eliminate Emotionally Anchored Distractors
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Confirmation BiasTendency to seek out and credit information that validates preexisting beliefs while discarding opposing facts.Ignoring 9 peer-reviewed papers to cite 1 fringe blog post.
Framing EffectDrawing different conclusions from the same information depending on how it is presented.'90% survival rate' sounds miraculous; '10% mortality rate' sounds terrifying.
Anchoring BiasOver-relying on the first piece of information encountered when making judgments.Treating an initial inflated budget estimate as the baseline for all decisions.
Bandwagon EffectBelieving a claim is true merely because a majority of people endorse it.'Millions of people believe this; therefore, it must be valid.'

Pedagogical Note: In TKA questions, identify when an author manipulates framing to elicit an instinctive emotional reaction rather than logical agreement.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Framing Effect
blocks.question: Policy A states: 'Our new tax policy ensures that 92% of households will experience no tax increase.' Policy B (opponents) states: 'This disastrous tax policy directly raises taxes on 8% of hard-working families!' Do these statements present different facts?
steps: Fakta Matematis: 92% rumah tangga tidak mengalami kenaikan pajak, 8% rumah tangga mengalami kenaikan pajak.
Perbedaan Framing: Policy A membingkai angka 92% sebagai kesuksesan mayoritas; Policy B membingkai angka 8% sebagai serangan bencana.
Kesimpulan: Ini adalah contoh nyata 'Framing Effect' di mana fakta yang sama dibungkus dengan sudut pandang emosional yang berlawanan.
blocks.answer: Kedua pernyataan menyajikan fakta yang persis sama, namun dibungkus dengan Framing Effect yang berlawanan.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: When a researcher conducts a study on organic food and systematically discards all laboratory results that fail to show nutritional superiority, what cognitive bias is committed?
blocks.hint: Membuang data yang membantah keyakinan pribadi adalah Confirmation Bias.
blocks.explanation: Tindakan memilih-milih data yang hanya mendukung hipotesis sendiri dan mengabaikan data yang bertentangan adalah wujud nyata dari 'Confirmation bias' (Pilihan B).

lessons.title: Evaluating Statistical Validity: Sample Size, Control Groups, and Correlation vs Causation

blocks.html:
Statistical Literacy: Unraveling Experimental Design

The cardinal sin of pop science reporting is confusing correlation (two variables fluctuating together) with causation (one variable directly creating the change in the other). Just because two variables correlate does not mean one caused the other.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: The Danger of Tiny Samples (12 Patients vs Global Millions)
blocks.html: In 1998, a fraudulent medical paper claimed a link between childhood vaccines and autism based on a study of only 12 children with zero control group. The paper was fully retracted after investigations exposed cherry-picked data. Discerning readers must audit statistical validity: A sensational claim supported by a handful of anecdotal cases is scientifically worthless.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Karl Popper on Empirical Falsifiability and Sample Sufficiency
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Karl Popper & Ronald Fisher Tahun: 1934 – 1935 M Krisis: Test-takers accept sweeping claims based on anecdotal personal experiences or unrepresentative mini-samples.

Philosopher of science Karl Popper (The Logic of Scientific Discovery, 1934) and statistician Ronald Fisher established the foundation of modern empirical research: A scientific hypothesis can never be verified by a few confirming instances; it requires rigorous testing with statistically adequate sample sizes, randomized controls, and confidence thresholds.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Statistical Sample Representativeness, Power, and Selection Bias
blocks.html:
Statistical Validity: The assurance that research conclusions accurately reflect real-world dynamics because the sample size is sufficiently large (statistical power) and randomly drawn without selection bias.

Selection Bias: Distortion arising when study participants are systematically unrepresentative of the broader target population (e.g., polling only Twitter users to predict a nationwide election).

blocks.title: Statistical Validity Diagnostic Checklist
blocks.html:
Sample Size Audit (N ≥ Threshold) → Randomization & Control Check → Correlation vs Causation Screen → Replication Verification
Diagnostic CheckPotential Flaw / VulnerabilityExample in Reading Tests
Sample Size (N)Sample too small to achieve statistical significance.'Only 15 employees were surveyed before restructuring the entire company.'
Selection BiasVoluntary or non-random participation.'An online poll where only angry customers bothered to respond.'
Correlation ≠ CausationAssuming simultaneous trends imply direct causation.'Ice cream sales and drowning rates both peak in July → Summer heat is the common cause.'
Lack of Control GroupNo comparison baseline to rule out placebo effects.'Patients felt better after taking herb X, but they also rested in bed for a week.'

Pedagogical Note: On critical reading questions, identify when an author commits the 'Hasty Generalization' fallacy by extrapolating from an unrepresentative sample.

blocks.title: Contoh Membedakan Korelasi dan Sebab-Akibat
blocks.question: A study discovers that people who sleep with their shoes on frequently wake up with severe headaches. A newspaper headlines: 'Sleeping with Shoes Causes Migraines!' Is this causal conclusion valid?
steps: Korelasi yang diamati: Tidur memakai sepatu berkorelasi dengan sakit kepala saat bangun.
Variabel Pengganggu Tersembunyi (Lurking Variable): Orang yang tidur masih memakai sepatu biasanya sedang dalam keadaan mabuk berat atau kelelahan ekstrem.
Penyebab Sebenarnya Sakit Kepala: Dehidrasi alkohol akibat mabuk, bukan sepatu itu sendiri.
Kesimpulan: Judul koran tersebut keliru menyimpulkan korelasi palsu (spurious correlation) sebagai hubungan sebab-akibat.
blocks.answer: Kesimpulan tersebut cacat karena mengabaikan variabel pengganggu (mabuk/kelelahan) dan keliru menetapkan sepatu sebagai penyebab sakit kepala.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Which research design feature is ESSENTIAL to prove that a new pharmaceutical drug directly cures an illness, rather than patients recovering naturally?

options.A: An active social media marketing campaign.
options.B: A randomized control group receiving an identical-looking placebo.
options.D: A colorful graphical poster in pharmacy windows.

blocks.hint: Kelompok kontrol dengan plasebo mutlak diperlukan untuk membuktikan efek obat.
blocks.explanation: Keberadaan kelompok kontrol acak yang menerima plasebo mutlak dibutuhkan untuk memisahkan efek biologis obat dari penyembuhan alami tubuh atau efek sugesti plasebo (Pilihan B).

lessons.title: Detecting Commercial Sponsorship and Covert Vested Interests

blocks.html:
Follow the Money: Vested Interests and Funding Bias

In academic critique, investigating conflicts of interest (COI) is mandatory. When a research study concluding that 'Sugary carbonated beverages pose zero dental or metabolic hazards' turns out to be funded entirely by an association of soft drink manufacturers, its objective credibility is deeply compromised.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Who Paid for the Research?
blocks.html: If you read a scientific report announcing: 'Eating sugar before bedtime causes no tooth decay and improves sleep quality', and at the bottom in tiny print it reveals: 'This research was funded by the Global Confectionery and Candy Manufacturers Association', what should happen to your trust in that study? It should drop to zero! Uncovering Covert Vested Interests is essential for critical literacy.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Chomsky, Herman, and the Propaganda Model
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Noam Chomsky & Edward S. Herman Tahun: 1988 M Krisis: Tobacco companies funded 'independent health institutes' to publish 'studies' claiming cigarettes were harmless, deceiving the public for decades.

In Manufacturing Consent: The Political Economy of the Mass Media (1988), Noam Chomsky and Edward Herman unveiled the corporate and advertiser filters that covertly shape public scientific narratives and policy agendas.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Conflict of Interest and Funding Bias
blocks.html: Conflict of Interest (COI) occurs when an individual or organization has competing professional or personal interests (such as financial gain from stock shares or sponsorships) that could compromise their scientific objectivity. Funding Bias is the proven empirical tendency of research studies to yield conclusions that favor their financial sponsors.

blocks.title: Checklist for Detecting Covert Vested Interests
blocks.html:
1. Inspect Funding Disclosures → 2. Examine Methodological Cherry-Picking → 3. Check Author Affiliations → 4. Compare with Independent Studies
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
1. Inspect Funding DisclosuresCheck footnotes for grants from pharmaceutical, fossil fuel, or tech lobbying groupsFollow the money
2. Examine Methodological Cherry-PickingWere unfavorable data sets conveniently omitted from the published graphs?Selective reporting
3. Check Author AffiliationsAre the lead scientists employed directly by the corporation marketing the product?Institutional capture
4. Compare with Independent StudiesDo publicly-funded university studies reach the opposite conclusion?Consensus cross-check

Pedagogical Note: When a passage discusses author bias: Point to commercial funding as the primary driver of compromised neutrality.

blocks.title: Mendeteksi Bias Pendanaan (Funding Bias)
blocks.html: Selalu periksa bagian 'Funding and Disclosure Statement' atau 'Acknowledgements' di akhir laporan ilmiah. Periksa apakah para peneliti menerima honorarium, saham, atau dana operasional dari korporasi yang produknya sedang diteliti.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Konflik Kepentingan
blocks.question: A whitepaper claims that an oil pipeline expansion poses 'absolute zero environmental risk to groundwater'. The report's authors are employed as senior corporate consultants for the petroleum pipeline consortium. How should a critical reader evaluate this source?
steps: Afiliasi Penulis: Konsultan korporasi senior pada konsorsium minyak yang bersangkutan.
Kepentingan Finansial: Penulis menerima kompensasi finansial langsung dari kelancaran proyek pipa minyak.
Klaim Laporan: Klaim absolut 'absolute zero environmental risk' sangat tidak realistis dalam rekayasa geoteknik pipa.
Kesimpulan: Terdapat konflik kepentingan finansial yang sangat nyata; laporan tersebut wajib diaudit ulang oleh tim ilmuwan independen non-profit.
blocks.answer: Laporan tersebut memiliki konflik kepentingan komersial berat yang merusak objektivitas independennya.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Why must researchers in medical trials explicitly declare all corporate financial sponsorships?

options.A: To comply with corporate taxation advertising laws.
options.B: To allow reviewers and the scientific community to evaluate potential funding bias and conflicts of interest.
options.C: To increase the market price of the drug in public pharmacies.
options.D: To ensure the laboratory staff receive bonus gifts.

blocks.hint: Deklarasi sponsor memungkinkan pengujian potensi bias pendanaan.
blocks.explanation: Deklarasi transparansi pendanaan memungkinkan komunitas ilmiah dan penelaah menguji potensi bias komersial atau konflik kepentingan dalam metodologi dan kesimpulan riset (Pilihan B).

lessons.title: Jebakan Fallacy of Authority vs Ad Hominem Dismissal

blocks.html:
Two Dangerous Extremes: Blind Adulation vs Petty Rejection

When critiquing information credibility, test takers frequently stumble into two mirror-image fallacies:

  1. Appeal to Unqualified Authority (Argumentum Ad Verecundiam): Menerima klaim sebagai kebenaran mutlak hanya karena diucapkan oleh orang terkenal atau berpangkat tinggi.
  2. Ad Hominem Dismissal: Menolak argumen yang valid dan terbukti benar hanya karena membenci kepribadian, penampilan, atau afiliasi politik sang pembicara.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: An Einstein Quote About Dental Hygiene?
blocks.html: Albert Einstein was an undisputed genius in theoretical physics. But if an advertisement quotes Einstein giving advice on toothpaste or cryptocurrency investing, does his physics brilliance make his financial advice reliable? No! This is the Fallacy of Appeal to False Authority. Conversely, rejecting someone's proven mathematical calculation simply because they are rude is the Ad Hominem Fallacy.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: John Locke and the Four Argument Categories
blocks.html:
Tokoh: John Locke Tahun: 1690 M Krisis: People reject a valid mathematical theorem because they dislike the mathematician's personality (Ad Hominem), or accept false dietary advice because an Olympic sprinter tweeted it (False Authority).

English philosopher John Locke in An Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1690) coined the term Argumentum ad Verecundiam (Appeal to Modesty / False Authority), alongside Argumentum ad Hominem, cautioning against bowing to prestigious names rather than examining empirical proof.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Argumentum ad Verecundiam vs Argumentum ad Hominem
blocks.html: Appeal to False Authority (Ad Verecundiam): Citing a famous figure whose expertise lies in a completely unrelated domain, or treating their word as infallible gospel. Ad Hominem: Attacking the person's character, appearance, ethnicity, or background rather than refuting the substantive logical merits of their argument.

blocks.title: Diagnostic Tests for Authority vs Ad Hominem
blocks.html:
Valid Authority → False Authority Fallacy → Ad Hominem Fallacy
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Valid AuthorityExpertise in the EXACT field under discussion + peer-reviewed consensus + unbiasedLegitimate expert warrant
False Authority FallacyCelebrity, politician, or athlete speaking outside their area of professional masteryIllegitimate prestige transfer
Ad Hominem Fallacy'His economic model is wrong because he has an annoying voice and is arrogant'Irrelevant personal attack

Pedagogical Note: In reading evaluations: Disqualify arguments that rest entirely on celebrity endorsements or personal character insults.

blocks.title: Patuhi Aturan Emas Logika Argumen
blocks.html: Sebuah argumen dievaluasi berdasarkan kekuatan bukti dan validitas penalarannya, bukan berdasarkan status selebritas pengusungnya (Appeal to Authority) dan bukan pula berdasarkan watak pribadi pembicaranya (Ad Hominem)!

blocks.title: Contoh Membedakan Kritik Argumen vs Ad Hominem
blocks.question:
Debate: Dr. Aris presents peer-reviewed radar telemetry showing ice shelf retreat.
Criticism A: 'Dr. Aris's telemetry methodology used an outdated satellite frequency with a 15% error margin.'
Criticism B: 'Dr. Aris was rude to his intern last week and wears unfashionable ties; therefore his radar data is false.'
steps: Kritik A: Kritik metodologis ilmiah yang sah (menguji frekuensi radar dan margin galat).
Kritik B: Cacat logika Ad Hominem (menyerang sikap pribadi dan pakaian Dr. Aris yang sama sekali tidak berhubungan dengan keabsahan data radar).
Kesimpulan: Kritik A adalah kritik valid; Kritik B adalah cacat logika Ad Hominem.
blocks.answer: Kritik A menyerang metodologi ilmiah (valid), sedangkan Kritik B menyerang kepribadian pribadi (Ad Hominem).

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Dismissing an internationally certified mathematical proof simply because the mathematician who formulated it has an irritable personality is an example of...
blocks.hint: Menyerang kepribadian alih-alih substansi argumen matematika adalah Ad Hominem.
blocks.explanation: Menolak pembuktian matematika yang sah hanya karena membenci kepribadian sang matematikawan merupakan contoh klasik kekeliruan logika 'Ad Hominem' (Pilihan B).

lessons.title: Critical Information Evaluation and Chapter Quiz

blocks.html:
Information Evaluation Capstone Drill

Put your critical information audit skills to work before tackling the chapter quiz:

  • Apply the CRAAP test: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, Purpose.
  • Distinguish domain expertise from celebrity endorsements.
  • Detect cognitive biases, framing manipulations, and lurking variables in correlations.
  • Identify funding conflicts of interest and avoid ad hominem dismissals.

blocks.title: Cheat Sheet: Logical Fallacy Field Guide & Source Audit
blocks.subtitle: Summary of 6 common logical fallacies, empirical vs anecdotal evidence, and detecting author bias.
blocks.html:
1. Top 6 Common Fallacies in TKA Passages

  • Ad Hominem: Attacking the opponent's personal traits rather than their substantive argument.
  • Straw Man: Oversimplifying or misrepresenting an opposing claim to make it easy to attack.
  • False Dilemma (Either/Or): Presenting two extreme options as the only possibilities when nuanced middle ground exists.
  • Slippery Slope: Falsely asserting that one minor event will inevitably trigger a chain of catastrophic consequences.
  • Post Hoc Ergo Propter Hoc: Assuming that because event B followed event A, event A must have caused event B.
  • Appeal to False Authority: Citing a celebrity or non-expert to endorse a complex technical claim.

2. Evaluating Evidence Strength

Empirical / Scientific > Anecdotal / Personal: Peer-reviewed studies, randomized controlled trials, and representative sample statistics always outweigh isolated personal testimonials.

blocks.text: Kuis Uji Kompetensi TKA Bahasa Inggris Tingkat Lanjut: Menilai Argumen dan Kredibilitas Informasi (20 Soal Pilihan Ganda Terstandar).
